title: Mapping Kenyon Cell Inputs in Drosophila Using Dye Electroporation
author: Ellis, Domagala, et al.
materials:
Timing: 45 min
4.Prepare the saline solution.a.Add the specified amount of the following chemicals to a 2 L single-use bottle: 12.62 g of NaCl, 0.75 g of KCl, 2.38 g of HEPES, 3.78 g of trehalose, 6.85 g of sucrose, 0.67 g of NaHCO3 and 0.24 g of NaH2PO4.b.Add 1,750 mL of deionized, filtered water to the same 2 L bottle and mix until the chemicals are dissolved.c.Add 4 mL of 1 M CaCl2 and 8 mL of 1 M MgCl2 to the solution and mix well.d.Add 310 μL of 10 M NaOH solution, one drop at a time, to the saline solution and mix after adding each drop.e.Add 238 mL of deionized, filtered water to the saline solution and mix well.f.Filter the resulting saline solution using a vacuum filtration system that has a polyesthersulfone membrane with a pore size of 0.22 mm (Corning).g.Use a pH meter to verify that the pH of the saline solution is approximately 7.3.h.Use an osmometer to verify that the osmolarity is within the optimal range: between 265 and 275 mOsm.i.Store at 4°C for up to one month.
Note: We use disposable spatulas, weigh boats, and 2 L bottles to prevent soap residue from contaminating the saline solution. We refrain from using a magnetic stir bar for the same reason. Instead, we mix the saline solution with a disposable serological pipette.
Note: The amount and the final concentration of each chemical is listed in a table in the materials and equipment section.
Note: We use the FiveEasyPlus™ pH meter (Mettler Toledo) to measure pH and the VAPRO® Vapor Pressure Osmometer (Wescor®) to measure osmolarity.
Note: The pH of the saline can be adjusted using NaOH (if it is too acidic 7.3). The osmolarity of the saline can be adjusted by adding trehalose (if it is too low 275 mOsm) (See problem 1 in the troubleshooting section).
5.Prepare the collagenase.a.Reconstitute the collagenase using saline to a final concentration of 2 mg/mL.b.Store at −20°C for up to 1 year.6.Prepare the fluorescent dye.a.Dilute 3000-Da Texas Red™ dextran dye using saline to a final concentration of 100 mg/mL.b.Store in the dark at −20°C.

steps.title: Generate transgenic flies
steps.instruction: Maintain D. melanogaster stocks carrying nSynaptobrevin‑GAL4 and UAS‑C3PAGFP transgenes using standard cornmeal agar at 25 °C, 60 % humidity, 12 h light/12 h dark. Collect adult flies 1–3 days after eclosion for experiments. (The same transgenes are available in D. sechellia and D. simulans and can be generated in other species.)

steps.title: Prepare saline, collagenase, dye
steps.instruction: Prepare 2 L saline: add 12.62 g NaCl, 0.75 g KCl, 2.38 g HEPES, 3.78 g trehalose, 6.85 g sucrose, 0.67 g NaHCO₃, 0.24 g NaH₂PO₄ to 1 750 mL deionized filtered water, mix, then add 4 mL 1 M CaCl₂ and 8 mL 1 M MgCl₂. Add 310 µL 10 M NaOH dropwise, mix after each drop, then add 238 mL deionized filtered water. Vacuum‑filter through a 0.22 mm PES membrane, verify pH ≈ 7.3 (FiveEasyPlus™ pH meter) and osmolarity 265–275 mOsm (VAPRO® Vapor Pressure Osmometer). Store at 4 °C up to 1 month. Reconstitute collagenase in the same saline to 2 mg/mL; store at –20 °C up to 1 year. Dilute 3000‑Da Texas Red™ dextran in saline to 100 mg/mL; store in the dark at –20 °C.

steps.title: Pull and fire‑polish electrodes
steps.instruction: Pull borosilicate glass (100 mm length, 1 mm OD, 0.5 mm ID) with filament using a P‑2000 laser‑based micropipette puller (Sutter Instruments) according to the parameters listed in the materials table. Fire‑polish each electrode tip with an MF‑900 micro‑forge (Narishige) following the manufacturer’s guide.

steps.title: Dissect and mount brain
steps.instruction: Line the lid and base of two 10 mm petri dishes with thin SYLGARD® and fill both with saline. Anesthetize a fly with CO₂, remove the head, cuticle, and excess trachea using forceps. Transfer the brain with a pre‑wet glass Pasteur pipette into 2 mg/mL collagenase; incubate ≈ 30 s, then move the brain to the lid of the dish. Orient the brain anterior side on SYLGARD®, posterior side up. Cut tungsten wire into small segments, make pins, and pin the brain through both optic lobes into the SYLGARD® so that both hemispheres lie level.

steps.title: Photo‑label selected Kenyon cell
steps.instruction: Place the dish under the two‑photon microscope (Ultima, Bruker) with the dorsal side facing the left‑side micromanipulator. Switch to a 60× objective. Configure the imaging software (live‑scan parameters from the materials table) and tune the laser to 925 nm to locate the mushroom‑body calyx and Kenyon‑cell somata. Zoom ≈ 32×, draw an ROI around the chosen soma, then set photo‑labeling parameters, tune the laser to 710 nm and collect 3–5 scans in single‑image mode. Return the laser to 925 nm, exit ROI, and stop live scan. Wait 10 min, then verify increased fluorescence of the targeted soma. Acquire a Z‑series covering the entire calyx (1 µm steps, digital zoom 2×) and record the number of claw‑shaped dendritic terminals. (Optional: repeat on the opposite hemisphere.)

steps.title: Electroporate dye into projection neurons
steps.instruction: Fill the non‑pulled end of a pulled electrode with the Texas Red™ dextran solution, flush the capillary with saline using a syringe equipped with a GE Life Sciences Whatman inorganic membrane filter and a MicroFil tip, and secure the electrode in a Warner holder on the head‑stage. Align the electrode first with the brain, then with the mushroom‑body calyx using the MPC‑365 micromanipulator (ROE‑200 mode 0 for coarse alignment, mode 1 for calyx alignment, mode 4 for electroporation). Set electrophysiology rig and imaging software to the live‑scan parameters (laser at 925 nm). For each claw: locate the claw, insert the electrode tip into its centre (verify tip is inside in all planes), deliver one or two pulses of 10–50 V (30 V works reliably) using an S88 Dual Output Square Pulse Stimulator (GRASS), and confirm that only a single projection‑neuron axon is labeled. Repeat for as many claws as possible (prefer proximal dorsal claws first). After filling, acquire a Z‑series of the entire calyx (digital zoom 2×).

steps.title: Score dye‑filled glomeruli and record data
steps.instruction: Remove the pins from the optic lobes, flip the brain so the posterior side contacts SYLGARD® and the anterior side faces the objective, then re‑pin and return to the two‑photon microscope. Configure imaging software for post‑dye imaging, set laser to 925 nm, and capture a Z‑series that includes the antennal lobe and the three clusters of projection‑neuron somata (anterior‑dorsal, lateral, ventral). Identify dye‑filled glomeruli using publicly available antennal‑lobe maps and note somata positions. Acquire a Z‑series of the mushroom‑body lobes (αβ, α'β', γ) at digital zoom 1.5×. Determine the Kenyon‑cell type by locating its bright axons and comparing to published lobe maps. Create a connectivity matrix table with one column for each of the 51 glomerulus types and one row per Kenyon cell; add columns for cell type, total claw count, and number of claws successfully filled. (Scoring can be paused and completed later.) Finally, re‑score the matrix: evaluate each sample five times for consensus, then evaluate each glomerulus column five times to ensure consistent identification.
